questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: ... is the movement of food from the blood into the tissues.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Assimilation is the movement of digested food/nutrients from the blood into the tissues where they are used.

subQuestions.questionText: An example of water-soluble vitamins:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Vitamin B1 (thiamine) is a water-soluble vitamin. Vitamins A, E and K are fat-soluble.

subQuestions.questionText: The end products of cellulose digestion in the rumen:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Cellulose is fermented in the rumen by microorganisms producing volatile fatty acids - acetic acid and propionic acid (and butyric acid).

subQuestions.questionText:
The intake of feed in ruminant farm animals involves the following:
(i) Animals use their snouts to gather feed.
(ii) Feed is partially chewed and mixed with saliva to form a bolus.
(iii) The tongue pushes the bolus backward down the oesophagus into the rumen.
(iv) Feed is later brought back for re-chewing.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The correct sequence for feed intake in ruminants is (ii), (iii) and (iv). Ruminants use their tongue (not snouts) to gather feed.

subQuestions.questionText: Narrow stalls used in intensive farming to keep pregnant sows throughout the period of 16 weeks:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Gestation crates are narrow stalls specifically designed to house pregnant sows during gestation.

subQuestions.questionText: Equipment used to restrain a large ruminant animal so that it can be given medication:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
A crush is the specific restraining equipment used to safely hold large ruminant animals during medical treatment, vaccination or examination.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following is NOT a sign of poor health in farm animals:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Animals being alert and lively is a sign of GOOD health. Dull/rough coats, pale membranes and difficult breathing are all signs of poor health.

options.B: Animals have dull and rough coats
options.C: Pale and dull membranes of the eyes

subQuestions.questionText:
The following descriptions refer to external parasites:
(i) Live on the skin of the host
(ii) May be transmitted to human beings through ingestion of infected meat
(iii) May secrete toxins
(iv) May damage the skin of farm animals
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
External parasites (i) live on the skin, (iii) may secrete toxins, and (iv) may damage the skin. Statement (ii) refers to internal parasites (e.g. tapeworms) transmitted via ingestion of infected meat.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the pictures below shows the normal foetal position? (Refer to Pictures A, B, C and D in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Picture C shows the normal foetal position with the foetus presenting head-first (anterior presentation) with forelegs extended.

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE is the CORRECT sequence of the reproductive stages?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The correct reproductive sequence is: Conception (fertilisation) → Gestation (pregnancy) → Parturition (birth) → Lactation (milk production).

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the following description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
COLUMN A: A: Osmosis; B: Diffusion
COLUMN B: Passive absorption of volatile fatty acids through the rumen wall
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B only (2 marks)
Diffusion is responsible for the passive absorption of volatile fatty acids through the rumen wall. Osmosis specifically refers to water movement across a semi-permeable membrane.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the following description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
COLUMN A: A: Thyroid regulators; B: Tranquilisers
COLUMN B: Chemical substances added to the feed of farm animals so that they become calm and eat more
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B only (2 marks)
Tranquilisers are the chemical substances added to feed to calm animals and increase feed intake. Thyroid regulators affect metabolism, not behaviour.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the following description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
COLUMN A: A: Bunching; B: Pawing
COLUMN B: The tendency of sheep to stand closer together during hot conditions
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A only (2 marks)
Bunching is the behaviour where sheep stand closely together during hot conditions to seek shade from each other. Pawing refers to scraping the ground with the hooves.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the following description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
COLUMN A: A: Ointment; B: Anthelmintic
COLUMN B: Chemicals used to kill ticks and mites
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: None (2 marks)
Neither ointments nor anthelmintics kill ticks and mites. Chemicals used to kill ticks and mites are called acaricides/dips. Anthelmintics kill internal parasites (worms), and ointments are topical applications.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the following description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
COLUMN A: A: Hermaphrodites; B: Freemartins
COLUMN B: Animals which have both male and female reproductive organs
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A only (2 marks)
Hermaphrodites are animals possessing both male and female reproductive organs. Freemartins are sterile female cattle born as twins to males.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The percentage of feed that has not been excreted by an animal.
subQuestions.memoText:
Digestibility coefficient/digestibility coefficiency (2 marks)
This measures the proportion of feed nutrients that have been absorbed/digested by the animal rather than excreted in faeces.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: An approach that combines the advantages of modern, traditional and complementary treatment to provide health care for farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Sustainable medication / Integrated disease management (2 marks)
Accept either term. This holistic approach integrates multiple methods for animal healthcare.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The failure of a cow to expel the placenta within 12 to 24 hours after parturition.
subQuestions.memoText:
Placenta retention / Retained placenta (2 marks)
This is a post-parturition condition that requires veterinary intervention.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The process of removing fertilised egg cells from a superior donor cow.
subQuestions.memoText:
Embryo flushing / Embryo harvesting (2 marks)
This is part of embryo transfer technology where fertilised eggs are collected from genetically superior donor cows.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The organelle in the mid-piece of a sperm cell supplying energy for movement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mitochondrion (2 marks)
Mitochondria in the mid-piece of the sperm cell produce ATP (energy) needed for tail movement and motility.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Nitrogen-free extract is a measure of the quality of protein in a feed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Biological value / BV (1 mark)
Biological value (BV) is the measure of protein quality. Nitrogen-free extract refers to easily digestible carbohydrates in feed.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: A balling gun is a device used to administer liquid medication to farm animals to treat internal parasites.
subQuestions.memoText:
Drenching gun / Dosing gun / Syringe (1 mark)
A drenching/dosing gun administers liquid medication. A balling gun is used for solid bolus/pill administration.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: Artificial insemination takes place when the bull is allowed to mount and service a cow.
subQuestions.memoText:
Natural mating / Copulation (1 mark)
Natural mating/copulation is when the bull physically mounts the cow. Artificial insemination involves manual deposition of semen into the female reproductive tract.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: The mesoderm is the outer germ layer from which skin, hooves and hair develop.
subQuestions.memoText:
Ectoderm (1 mark)
The ectoderm is the outer germ layer that gives rise to skin, hooves, hair and the nervous system. The mesoderm forms muscles and bones.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD(S) to make the statement TRUE: The stage of parturition during which the calf is pushed out is known as preparatory.
subQuestions.memoText:
Ejection / Delivery / Expulsion (1 mark)
The expulsion/ejection/delivery stage is when the calf is actively pushed out. The preparatory stage involves uterine contractions before active labour.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the stage of development of the ruminant farm animal represented by DIAGRAM A. (Refer to the diagrams of stomach compartments of two ruminant farm animals in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Young ruminant farm animal (1 mark)
Diagram A shows the stomach of a young ruminant where the abomasum is dominant and the rumen is underdeveloped.

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons that are visible in the diagram above to support the answer to QUESTION 2.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Presence of oesophageal groove
• Underdeveloped fore-stomach (rumen/reticulum/omasum)
• Large abomasum
[Award 2 marks for any 2 correct reasons]

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify, in the diagrams above, the part where EACH of the following occurs (write only the letter):
(a) Feed is fermented
(b) Channelling of milk into the abomasum
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) D (1 mark) - The rumen is where feed is fermented by microorganisms.
(b) C (1 mark) - The oesophageal groove channels milk directly into the abomasum, bypassing the rumen in young ruminants.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate ONE adaptation feature of part E that enables it to absorb water from food.
subQuestions.memoText:
It has folds/leaves that squeeze water from the feed (1 mark)
The omasum has many folds (manyplies/leaves) that increase the surface area for water absorption.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the part in the alimentary canal of a fowl that corresponds with part F above in terms of functioning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Proventriculus / Glandular stomach (1 mark)
The proventriculus in fowls produces digestive enzymes and acids similar to the abomasum (true stomach) in ruminants.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the energy represented by A. (Refer to the schematic representation of energy flow of feed in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Metabolic energy / Metabolisable energy / ME (1 mark)
Metabolic energy = Digestible energy minus energy lost through urine and gases.

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the digestible energy of this feed. Include the formula. Gross energy = 850 joules; Energy lost through faeces = 255 joules.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: DE = Gross Energy − Energy lost through faeces
Mark 2: Substitution: DE = 850 joules − 255 joules
Mark 3: Answer: DE = 595 joules
[Award 3 marks for correct formula, substitution and answer]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the importance of the energy, represented by B, in animal production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
• For growth/production/reproduction/work
• For maintenance

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO aims of calculating the energy value of the feed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• To determine animal diet
• To determine feeding standards
• To determine ration formulation

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the purpose for which FEED B can be used based on its nutritive ratio. (Feed B has DP 39%, NR 1:4)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
• For growth
• For production
• For reproduction
[Feed B has a narrow NR of 1:4, indicating high protein - suitable for productive purposes]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.3.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
It has a high protein content (39%) / narrow NR (less than 1:6) (1 mark)
A narrow nutritive ratio indicates a protein-rich feed suitable for productive purposes.

subQuestions.questionText: Use the Pearson square method to calculate the ratio into which FEED A and FEED B should be mixed to get a feed with 16% DP. (Feed A has 8% DP; Feed B has 39% DP)
subQuestions.memoText:
Pearson square method:
Mark 1: Place desired protein (16%) in the centre
Mark 2: Feed A (8%) on one corner; difference 39−16 = 23 parts of Feed A
Mark 3: Feed B (39%) on other corner; difference 16−8 = 8 parts of Feed B
Mark 4: Ratio Feed A : Feed B = 23 : 8

        Feed A 8% ─────── 23 parts
                  ╲   ╱
                   16%
                  ╱   ╲
        Feed B 39% ────── 8 parts

[Award 4 marks total: correct setup, correct subtractions for both feeds, correct final ratio]

subQuestions.questionText:
Complete the table below by naming the minerals, vitamins and deficiency symptoms.
(a) Mineral with deficiency: Parakeratosis
(b) Deficiency symptom of Vitamin A
(c) Deficiency symptom of Cobalt
(d) Vitamin with deficiency: Poor blood clotting
(e) Mineral/vitamin with deficiency: Anaemia
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Zinc / Zn (1 mark)
(b) Night blindness / keratomalacia / malformation of bones / lower disease resistance / lower fertility / loss of appetite / diarrhoea (1 mark - any one)
(c) Wasting disease / stunted growth / poor appetite / listlessness / drop in milk production / anaemia / cardiac failure / infertility (1 mark - any one)
(d) Vitamin K (1 mark)
(e) Iron / Fe / Copper / Cu / vitamin B6 (1 mark - any one)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the component of feed most suitable for: Acts as solvent.
subQuestions.memoText:
Water (1 mark)
Water is the universal solvent in animal nutrition, dissolving nutrients and waste products.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the component of feed most suitable for: Fattening of farm animals for slaughter.
subQuestions.memoText:
Carbohydrates (1 mark)
Carbohydrates provide easily metabolisable energy for fat deposition during fattening.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the component of feed most suitable for: Easy absorption of fat-soluble vitamins and calcium.
subQuestions.memoText:
Fats / Oils / Lipids (1 mark)
Fats/oils/lipids are required as carriers/solvents for fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and assist in calcium absorption.

subQuestions.questionText: Classify the types of feeds represented by A and B. (Refer to the schematic representation of types of feeds in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Feed type A - Concentrates
Mark 2: Feed type B - Roughages
[Award 1 mark each]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify C above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Carbohydrate-rich concentrates (1 mark)
C represents carbohydrate-rich concentrates (energy-rich concentrates), which along with protein-rich concentrates form the concentrates category.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO functions of B (roughages) in animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Enhance the development of rumen in young animals
• Stimulate milk production
• Provide bulkiness to the ration
• Prevent bloating in ruminants
• Improve digestion
• Provide energy

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO feed examples of D (succulent roughages).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Silage
• Green fodder / pastures / soilage
• Green lucerne

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the animal production systems represented by FARM A and FARM B above. (Farm A: 320 Ha, 30 labourers, 3 big tractors, 1200 animals. Farm B: 850 Ha, 8 labourers, 1 small tractor + donkey cart, 103 animals.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: FARM A - Intensive production system
Mark 2: FARM B - Extensive production system
[Farm A has high inputs and high stocking density; Farm B has low inputs and low stocking density on a large area]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the production system identified in FARM B above in terms of space and the number of farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Space - Large space (850 Ha)
Mark 2: Number of animals - Fewer animals (only 103)
[Extensive systems are characterised by low stocking densities on large land areas]

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the table above to indicate the high inputs for FARM A.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
• 30 labourers
• 3 × big tractors
• Abattoir with equipment

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO ways in which the farmer at FARM B can increase animal productivity.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Correct feeding/nutrition/diet
• Improving environment/provision of shelter
• Breeding disease-resistant animals
• General production enterprise management

subQuestions.questionText:
Match the pictures (A–C) with the intensive production systems ((a)–(c)):
(a) Deep-litter system
(b) Free-range system
(c) Battery system
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Deep-litter system - Picture C (1 mark)
(b) Free-range system - Picture A (1 mark)
(c) Battery system - Picture B (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO important reasons for shelters for farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• To reduce effects of extreme weather conditions
• Protect against predators/theft
• Easy management
• Improved production

subQuestions.questionText: Name the purpose of the equipment in the broiler facility represented by A above (curtains).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
• Control light intensity
• Regulate the temperature inside the house / ventilation

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO other pieces of equipment that can be used to control temperature for chicks.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Insulators / bedding
• Heating equipment (when it is cold)
• Cooling equipment / ventilators (when it is hot)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors to consider when building a facility such as the one above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Orientation of the building
• Should allow air flow / ventilation
• Slope to allow good drainage / prevent run-off water entering
• Side walls should be insulated
• Cost effective
• Durability / strength
• Insulated roofing material

subQuestions.questionText: Use the information in the table above to identify A, B, C and D. (Table on diseases - Foot-and-mouth disease pathogen A; Tuberculosis symptoms B; Redwater pathogen C; Disease D caused by fungus with ring-like lesions)
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Virus (1 mark) [Foot-and-mouth disease is caused by a virus]
B - Chronic cough / Squeaky breathing / Dyspnea / Enlarged lymph nodes (1 mark - any one) [Symptoms of TB]
C - Protozoa (1 mark) [Redwater is caused by protozoa - Babesia]
D - Ringworm (1 mark) [Fungal infection causing ring-like lesions]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the vector represented by E (vector of heart water).
subQuestions.memoText:
Bont tick / 3-host tick (1 mark)
The bont tick (Amblyomma hebraeum) is the vector for heartwater disease.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO financial implications of animal diseases.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Decreased production / income / profit
• Banning of exports / international trade decreases
• Have negative impact on food security
• High cost to control / prevention

subQuestions.questionText: Identify, in the table above, the disease that can be transmitted from animals to human beings.
subQuestions.memoText:
Tuberculosis / TB / Ringworm (1 mark)
Both TB and ringworm are zoonotic diseases that can be transmitted from animals to humans.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the method to administer the medication above (Cinmycormion package insert).
subQuestions.memoText:
Intramuscular injection (1 mark)
The package insert specifies 'Intramuscular injection 2 mℓ/10 kg live body weight'.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify in the package insert above the role of the state in medication production.
subQuestions.memoText:
Registration of the medication / Reg. No. F 2144 / ACT 36/1947 (1 mark)
The state regulates and registers veterinary medications under Act 36 of 1947 (Fertilisers, Farm Feeds, Agricultural Remedies and Stock Remedies Act).

subQuestions.questionText: The products of animals treated with the above medication cannot be consumed within two weeks of treatment. Justify this statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
The medication is retained in the body for four weeks (1 mark)
Since the medication remains in the animal's body for 4 weeks, products (meat/milk) consumed within this period would contain medication residues, hence the withdrawal period.

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO other methods that can be used to administer medication through injection.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Intravenous injection
• Subcutaneous / hypodermic injection
• Intradermal injection
• Intraperitoneal injection
• Intraruminal injection
• Intramammary injection

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the poisonous plant shown in the pictures above.
subQuestions.memoText: Thorn apple / Devil's apple / Jamestown weed / Jimson weed / Stinkweed / Devil's trumpet / Datura stramonium (1 mark - accept any of these names)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO measures a farmer can take to prevent plant poisoning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Remove the poisonous plant
• Remove animals from camps infested with poisonous plant
• Avoid overgrazing / practice rotational grazing
• Feed animals well
• Inspection of hay provided to farm animals

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO ways in which farmers can treat farm animals that consumed the plant identified in QUESTION 3.6.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Keep affected animal away from drinking water for two days, thereafter allow only small quantities of water
• Administer activated charcoal / strong tea / tannic acid / remedies that will neutralise the plant poison
• Provide large doses of purgative to expel poison
• Dose the animal with sugar / glucose

subQuestions.questionText: Identify B and C. (Refer to the diagram of the reproductive system of a male farm animal in the question paper, showing parts A, B and C.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: B - Scrotum
Mark 2: C - Epididymis
[Award 1 mark each for correct identification]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the hormone secreted by A (testis).
subQuestions.memoText:
Testosterone (1 mark)
The testis secretes testosterone, the primary male reproductive hormone responsible for sperm production and male secondary characteristics.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the condition that occurs when A (testis) remains in the body cavities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cryptorchidism (1 mark)
Cryptorchidism is the condition where one or both testes fail to descend from the body cavity into the scrotum, often causing infertility.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the role of B (scrotum) in regulating the temperature of A (testis) in male farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: In hot conditions the scrotum relaxes moving the testes away from the body
Mark 2: In cooler conditions the scrotum contracts pulling the testes closer to the body
[The scrotum thermoregulates to keep testes 2-3°C below body temperature for optimal spermatogenesis]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO methods that can be used to collect semen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Both of the following (1 mark each):
• Artificial vagina
• Electrical stimulation / electro-ejaculator

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO requirements for the collection of semen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• All equipment that will be used should be readily available
• Equipment must be hygienic / clean / sterilised
• Floor area must not be slippery
• Personnel must be trained / skilled with experience / expertise
• Vial must be kept warm before and after collection
• Enough handlers should be available
• Teaser cow should be available
• Semen must not be exposed to direct sunlight

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO functions of semen dilutants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Provide nutrients / energy to the sperm cells
• Prevent contamination by micro-organisms
• Protect sperm cells against pH changes
• Protect sperm cells during freezing and thawing
• Increase the volume of semen
• Maintain proper osmotic / electrolyte pressure
• Increase the viability of the sperm cells

subQuestions.questionText: State the temperature required for storing semen in liquid nitrogen for a longer period of time.
subQuestions.memoText:
−196 °C (1 mark)
Liquid nitrogen storage at −196°C cryopreserves semen indefinitely while maintaining sperm viability.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the process illustrated in the diagram above. (Refer to the diagram of cell division during reproduction in the question paper showing oogonium developing into ovum and bipolar cells.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Oogenesis / Ovigenesis (1 mark)
Oogenesis is the process of egg cell (ovum) formation from oogonia in the ovary.

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the type of cell division responsible for the formation of the following:
(a) Cells labelled B
(b) Cells labelled A
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) B - Meiosis (1 mark) [Reduction division producing haploid gametes]
(b) A - Mitosis (1 mark) [Cell division producing diploid daughter cells]

subQuestions.questionText: State the purpose of the cell division in QUESTION 4.3.2(a). (Meiosis)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
• Reduce the number of chromosomes from diploid (2n) to haploid (n)
• To form gametes

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the organ where EACH of the following cells are found:
(a) Spermatogonium
(b) Oogonium
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Spermatogonium - Testis (1 mark)
(b) Oogonium / Oögonia - Ovary (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Draw a combined bar graph representing the butter fat and crude fibre percentages for weeks 5–25 of lactation. (Data: Week 5: BF 4.3%, CF 4.1%; Week 10: BF 4.4%, CF 4.2%; Week 15: BF 4.4%, CF 4.3%; Week 20: BF 4.5%, CF 4.4%; Week 25: BF 4.5%, CF 4.6%)
subQuestions.memoText:
Marking criteria/rubric (1 mark each, 6 marks total):
• Correct heading (e.g. 'Butterfat and crude fibre percentage from week 5–25 of lactation')
• X-axis: correct calibrations and labelled (Time)
• Y-axis: correct calibrations and labelled (Butterfat and crude fibre)
• Correct units (% and weeks)
• Bar graph (combined/grouped bars showing both BF and CF for each week)
• Accuracy (80%+ correctly plotted)

[The bars should show: Week 5 (BF 4.3, CF 4.1), Week 10 (BF 4.4, CF 4.2), Week 15 (BF 4.4, CF 4.3), Week 20 (BF 4.5, CF 4.4), Week 25 (BF 4.5, CF 4.6). Y-axis should range 0 to ~5%, include legend distinguishing butterfat from crude fibre]

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce, from the table above, the trend of crude fibre from weeks 25 to 45.
subQuestions.memoText:
Increases from 4.6 to 5.0 (1 mark)
Crude fibre percentage shows an increasing/upward trend from week 25 (4.6%) to week 45 (5.0%).

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down only the letter (A to F) of the part in the picture above that matches each of the following descriptions: (Refer to the illustration of the developing embryo in the uterus of a cow in the question paper.)
(a) The part that brings the blood of the cow and the foetus in close contact without mixing it
(b) The membrane that collects the urine from the foetus
(c) The membrane surrounding the foetus closest to the uterus of the cow
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) F (1 mark) [Placenta - exchange of nutrients/gases without blood mixing]
(b) B (1 mark) [Allantois - collects urine/waste from foetus]
(c) C (1 mark) [Chorion - outermost membrane next to uterus wall]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO functions of part D (amniotic fluid).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Shock absorber / prevents injuries
• Allow movement of the foetus
• Regulates temperature of the foetus
• Lubricates birth canal
• Prevents dehydration / desiccation of foetus

subQuestions.questionText: Name the milk that is produced during the first three days after parturition.
subQuestions.memoText:
Colostrum / Beestings (1 mark)
Colostrum is the first milk produced after parturition, rich in antibodies and nutrients essential for the newborn.

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why it is important that a newborn calf receives the milk named in QUESTION 4.6.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Antibodies increase disease resistance in calf
• Calcium and Phosphorus required for strong bone development
• Contains growth factors
• Assists in the maturation of the alimentary canal
• Richer in nutrients
• Serves as a laxative
• Higher in energy

subQuestions.questionText: Give the term that refers to the period when milk production is at its highest point.
subQuestions.memoText:
Peak period / Peak production (1 mark)
Peak production/peak period is when daily milk yield reaches its maximum during the lactation cycle, typically 4-8 weeks after calving in dairy cows.
